title: JSON with System.Text.Json
summary: Converting objects to and from JSON with JsonSerializer - serialising records and collections, options for naming, indentation and enums, attributes like JsonPropertyName and JsonIgnore, deserialising safely with nullable results and validation, reading unknown JSON with JsonDocument and JsonNode, and saving settings files.

cards.a:
When the JSON text is the literal null

Invalid JSON throws a JsonException, and missing properties are just left at their defaults. Only the JSON text `null` gives null.

cards.q: How do you make the JSON use camelCase names for PascalCase properties?
cards.a:
Set PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase in JsonSerializerOptions

The naming policy renames properties when writing (and reading). Case-insensitive only affects reading, and by default the names are written as declared. `[JsonPropertyName]` renames single properties.

cards.q: A JSON object lacks a property that the record has. What does Deserialize do by default?
cards.a:
Leaves that property at its default value (null, 0, false)

Missing properties are not an error unless you require them.
